title: the operator inbox shows falsifier clauses one per line
intention: cairn operator show renders a falsifier's clauses as '(n) claim' lines, wrapped, followed by wrong_intent and horizon when present, so Akien reads the clauses rather than a Python list repr.
why: Measured 2026-11-05: cairn/tools/operator_inbox/inbox.py:1191-1194 prints each dict falsifier value with f'{k}: {v}', so a clauses list would print as a Python list repr. The parent e4f02a1ceef5 makes the ticket plan JSON at the cast door (Akien 2026-11-05: 'should be json'); this reader must read the new shape before the door admits it.
traces_to: Law 4 and Law 1 via parent e4f02a1ceef5; RULE 1 (each reader's change lives in its own component).
how: In the FALSIFIER block, a dict carrying a clauses list renders each clause via _wrap(f'({n}) {claim}', '  ', width), then wrong_intent and horizon as labelled lines; other shapes unchanged; red-first proof.
falsifier: (1) a doc with falsifier {clauses: [{n:1, claim:'a'}, {n:2, claim:'b'}], horizon:'h'} renders lines '  (1) a', '  (2) b' and a horizon line, and no '[{' anywhere in the FALSIFIER block; (2) a {proves_green, proves_red} doc and a string doc render byte-identical to HEAD.
